terms.gloss: with a genitive, the seat of an activity: a centre, an office
evidence: M-O s.v. tourist office, information office, visitors’ center: sēdēs nūntiātiōnum, citing Egger
M-O s.v. office: officiōrum sēdēs, citing Egger
terms.comment: Classically a seat or dwelling, the place where something has its home (Lewis & Short). Where Latin has a name for the place, use it: a sports centre is a gymnasium, a health centre a valētūdinārium (see gym, hospital).

terms.gloss: a meeting place; a community or conference centre
terms.comment: In Livy the market and meeting place of a country district. Plautus uses it as a joke for a brothel (Trin. 2.2.38, Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: sedes · Lewis & Short: conciliabulum
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. office; tourist office, information office, visitors’ center; convention center.
